limitations_and_boundaries: The mechanism of nicotine accumulation in the intestine is not addressed.
The study does not demonstrate causality between B. xylanisolvens abundance and NAFLD in humans; only correlations are shown.
The clinical cohort is relatively small (83 patients) and limited to biopsy-proven NAFLD.
The long-term safety and efficacy of B. xylanisolvens as a therapeutic intervention are not evaluated.
The study focuses on nicotine-associated NASH; generalizability to other NAFLD etiologies is unknown.
The role of other gut bacteria in nicotine degradation is not explored.
The in vivo experiments are limited to mouse models; human intervention trials are lacking.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.
